claim.date_text_original: Ibn Battuta visit to Taghaza, AH 753 / 1352 CE
claim.summary: During his 1352 crossing of the Sahara, Ibn Battuta described Taghaza as inhabited by enslaved people of the Massufa who dug the salt. The atlas records a bounded site-level slavery-and-mining-labor observation for 1352, without extending it to the Massufa as a whole, the trans-Saharan network as a territorial practice surface, or an indefinite period.
claim.notes: The English translation uses 'slaves' for the workers. The Atlas preserves the bounded translated testimony and specialist reuse of the passage, but does not infer ownership structure, exact worker counts, hereditary status, or continuous practice beyond the observed context.

territorial_practice.notes: Site-level 1352 classification only. No P-level, population estimate, continuous duration, Massufa-wide prevalence, or network-derived territorial polygon.
